title: improv·artist · tender (Felix Gonzalez-Torres)
mutation_directive: improv artist: tender via Felix Gonzalez-Torres

improv_extras.practice: candy spills, light strings, paired clocks; intimacy as sculpture

v1.feedback: The Aizawa attractor reads clearly within 2 seconds and the warm amber palette is genuinely restrained — single-hue with age-driven brightness is the right call for Gonzalez-Torres's incandescent intimacy. The 'release' mechanic where aged particles drift downward and fade is a legible sculptural gesture that maps well to the letting-go theme. However, the breathing modulation is too subtle to register visually — push uBreath higher or make the paired-clock drift between two attractor parameter states more pronounced so the viewer can feel two rhythms slowly desynchronizing. The centroid-tracking camera keeps framing tight, which is good, but consider a slower, more meditative orbit speed to match the tender register — right now the rotation feels slightly mechanical against the emotional intent.

v2.feedback: The two-clock desync concept maps well to Gonzalez-Torres's paired clocks, and the candy-spill gravity on aged particles is a genuine design move, not decoration. However, the Aizawa attractor's inherent shape dominates — the two halves read as one fuzzy torus rather than two distinct paired forms, so the 'two clocks' concept is legible only if you already know the UV split. To sharpen the pairing, spatially offset clock A and clock B into two distinct clusters (like his actual paired clocks hung side by side) and let the breath desync be visible as shape divergence rather than buried in parameter modulation. The releasing particles drift downward but dissipate before accumulating into a readable candy-pile floor — add a slower fade or a ground-plane accumulation pass so the spill metaphor actually lands visually.
